question: Test Yourself 1: A plastic shatter-resistant face shield:
choices: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

question: Test Yourself 2: More than half of all crashes:
choices: Occur at speeds greater than 35mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders who have less than five months of experience on their motorcycles.

question: Test Yourself 3: When riding, you should:
choices: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.

question: Test Yourself 4: Usually, a good way to handle tailgaters is to:
choices: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.

question: Test Yourself 5: To reduce your reaction time, you should:
choices: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch lever and the brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

question: Test Yourself 6: Making eye contact with other drivers:
choices: Is a good sign they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Doesn't mean that the driver will yield.
Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you.

question: Test Yourself 7: Reflective clothing should:
choices: Be worn at night.
Be worn during the day.
Not be worn.
Be worn day and night

question: Test Yourself 8: The best way to stop quickly is to:
choices: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

question: Test Yourself 9: When it starts to rain it is usually best to:
choices: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

question: Test Yourself 10: If your motorcycle starts to wobble:
choices: Accelerate out of the wobble.
Use the brakes gradually.
Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
Downshift.

question: Test Yourself 11: If you are chased by a dog:
choices: Kick it away.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

question: Test Yourself 12: Passengers should:
choices: Lean as you lean.
Hold on to the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

question: Test Yourself 13: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:
choices: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the leader.

question: Test Yourself 14: If you wait one hour per drink for the alcohol to be eliminated from your body before riding:
choices: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Side effects from the drinking may still remain.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

question: Knowledge Test (Sample Questions) 1: It is MOST important to flash your brake light when:
choices: Someone is following too closely.
You will be slowing suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

question: Knowledge Test (Sample Questions) 2: The FRONT brake supplies how much of the potential stopping power?
choices: About 25%.
About 50%.
At least 70%.
All of the stopping power.

question: Knowledge Test (Sample Questions) 3: To swerve correctly:
choices: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

question: Knowledge Test (Sample Questions) 4: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:
choices: Relax on the handgrips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

question: Knowledge Test (Sample Questions) 5: The car below is waiting to enter the intersection. It is best to: (picture: car waiting at a side street)
choices: Make eye contact with the driver.
Reduce speed and be ready to react.
Maintain speed and position.
Maintain speed and move right.
